## Overview

<div class="glmap-eli5-box">
<span class="glmap-box-badge">🌱 ELI5 (3 Golden Rules to Switch from Leaflet)</span><br/>
Switching an existing R script or Shiny app from <code>leaflet</code> to <code>glmap</code> takes three simple habits:
<ol>
<li>Replace <code>leaflet() |&gt; addProviderTiles(...)</code> with <b><code>glmap(basemap = "dark")</code></b> (or <code>"positron"</code>).</li>
<li>Delete <code>pal &lt;- colorNumeric(...)</code> and <code>addLegend(...)</code>—just pass <b><code>color = ~column, palette = "viridis"</code></b> directly into <code>add_points()</code> or <code>add_polygons()</code>.</li>
<li>In Shiny, replace <code>leafletOutput</code> / <code>renderLeaflet</code> / <code>leafletProxy</code> with <b><code>glmapOutput</code> / <code>renderGlmap</code> / <code>glmap_proxy</code></b>.</li>
</ol>
</div>

<div class="glmap-tech-box">
<span class="glmap-box-badge">⚙️ Technical Mode (API &amp; Reactivity Mapping)</span><br/>
<code>glmap</code> was designed so that R users and AI coding agents familiar with <code>leaflet</code> can transition immediately while gaining <b>100x–500x faster C++17 binary serialization</b> and <b>60 FPS WebGL2 GPU rendering</b>. All functions use consistent <code>snake_case</code>, evaluate tidy/formula aesthetics (<code>~expr</code>) via C/R 256-entry RGB lookup tables, and emit <code>leaflet</code>-compatible Shiny input events (<code>_click</code>, <code>_bounds</code>, <code>_zoom</code>, <code>_marker_click</code>, <code>_shape_click</code>).
</div>

---

## Complete Function-by-Function Mapping

| `leaflet` Function | `glmap` Function | Key Parameter Differences |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `leaflet(data)` | `glmap(data, basemap = "dark")` | Includes basemap out of the box (`"dark"`, `"positron"`, `"voyager"`, `"osm"`, `"satellite"`) |
| `addTiles()` / `addProviderTiles()` | `set_basemap("positron")` | Or set `basemap =` directly in `glmap()` |
| `addCircleMarkers()` / `addMarkers()` | `add_points()` | `lng` $\rightarrow$ `lon`, `fillOpacity` $\rightarrow$ `opacity`, pass `color = ~col, palette = "viridis"` directly |
| `addLabelOnlyMarkers()` | `add_labels()` | `label` $\rightarrow$ `text` |
| `addPolylines()` | `add_lines()` | `weight` $\rightarrow$ `width` |
| `addPolygons()` | `add_polygons()` | `fillColor` $\rightarrow$ `fill_color`, `fillOpacity` $\rightarrow$ `fill_opacity`, `color` $\rightarrow$ `line_color`, `weight` $\rightarrow$ `line_width` |
| `addRasterImage()` | `add_raster()` | Streams raw `Float32` values to GPU shader; supports `hillshade = TRUE` and live UI palette switching |
| `addHeatmap()` (`leaflet.extras`) | `add_heatmap()` | Built-in WebGL2 additive Gaussian kernel shader |
| *(No built-in equivalent)* | `add_hexbin()` | Built-in C++17 64-bit hexagonal spatial aggregation for 1M+ points |
| `setView(lng, lat, zoom)` | `set_view(lng, lat, zoom, pitch, bearing)` | Supports 3D camera `pitch` and `bearing` |
| `flyTo(lng, lat, zoom)` | `fly_to(lng, lat, zoom, pitch, bearing)` | Smooth WebGL camera animation |
| `fitBounds(lng1, lat1, lng2, lat2)` | `fit_bounds(c(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax))` | Also accepts an `sf` or `SpatRaster` object directly |
| `leafletOutput()` / `renderLeaflet()` | `glmapOutput()` / `renderGlmap()` | Drop-in Shiny UI & Server replacements |
| `leafletProxy()` | `glmap_proxy()` | Supports `clear_layer()`, `clear_layers()`, `set_layer_visibility()`, `set_layer_opacity()`, `set_raster_style()`, `set_filter()` |

## Side-by-Side Migration Examples

### Example 1: Polygons Colored by a Continuous Attribute

#### `leaflet`
```r
library(leaflet)

pal <- colorNumeric("viridis", domain = nc$BIR74)

leaflet(nc) |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) |>
  addPolygons(
    fillColor = ~pal(BIR74),
    fillOpacity = 0.75,
    color = "#ffffff",
    weight = 1,
    popup = ~NAME
  ) |>
  addLegend("bottomright", pal = pal, values = ~BIR74, title = "Births 1974")
```

#### `glmap`
```{r}
library(glmap)

glmap(nc, basemap = "positron") |>
  add_polygons(
    fill_color = ~BIR74,
    palette = "viridis",
    fill_opacity = 0.75,
    line_color = "#ffffff",
    line_width = 1,
    popup = ~NAME
  )
```

---

### Example 2: `terra::SpatRaster` with Live Interactive Shader Controls

#### `leaflet`
```r
# Projects and renders a static PNG in R on the CPU; changing colors requires re-running R
pal <- colorNumeric("terrain", values(dem), na.color = "transparent")
leaflet() |>
  addTiles() |>
  addRasterImage(dem, colors = pal, opacity = 0.8)
```

#### `glmap`
```{r}
# Uploads raw Float32 values to GPU texture; user can switch palettes & toggle hillshade at 0ms in browser
glmap(basemap = "dark") |>
  add_raster(dem, palette = "terrain", hillshade = TRUE, opacity = 0.8)
```
